hints: Focus on the strict definition, structural isomers must have the same molecular formula but different structural arrangement.
Count atoms carefully for pair 1, both have 6 carbons, 12 hydrogens and 2 oxygens, but one is an acid and one is an ester.
For pair 3, number the longest chain from each end to find the position of the OH group and see if they are really different.
walkthrough:
**Recall what counts as structural isomers**

Structural isomers have identical molecular formulae but different connectivity. That can be a different carbon skeleton, different functional group, or different position of the same group.

Rule to test:
$$\text{same molecular formula + different structure = structural isomers}$$

**Test pair 1, acid versus ester**

First molecule: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ has 6 C, 12 H, 2 O, so $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_2$.

Second molecule: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ also has 6 C, 12 H, 2 O, so $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_2$. One is a carboxylic acid, the other is an ester, so connectivity is different. Pair 1 is a pair of functional group isomers.

**Test pair 2, branched alkanes**

Left structure is 2,3-dimethylbutane. Right structure is 3-methylpentane.

Both have formula:
$$\text{C}_6\text{H}_{14}$$
But the carbon branching is different, so they are chain isomers. Pair 2 is correct.

**Test pair 3, same alcohol written two ways**

Left: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ is hexan-3-ol.

Right: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ is also hexan-3-ol. The OH is on carbon 3 in both cases when you number to give the lowest locant. They are the identical molecule, not isomers. So only 1 and 2 are correct.

options.A: Incorrect because it includes 3. Pair 3 molecules are both hexan-3-ol, just written left to right versus right to left. Identical compounds cannot be isomers of each other.
options.B: Correct because 1 and 2 only are structural isomers. Pair 1 is acid versus ester with formula C6H12O2. Pair 2 is 2,3-dimethylbutane versus 3-methylpentane with formula C6H14.
options.C: Incorrect because it includes 3 and omits 1. Pair 1 is valid (same formula, different functional group) and pair 3 is invalid (same compound).
options.D: Incorrect because it omits 2. Pair 2 molecules both have formula C6H14 but different branching, so they are genuine chain isomers and must be included.
